args.fix: Lock accounts in globally consistent ascending-id order (with self-transfer special case) instead of sender-then-receiver, preserving all return values/exceptions while eliminating the lock-ordering cycle.
args.root_cause: transfer() did SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on sender then receiver in request order. Concurrent opposite transfers (A->B vs B->A) each hold one row lock and block on the other, forming a deadlock cycle that Postgres aborts with 'deadlock detected'.

text: Fix accepted: ordered row locking (`min(id)` first) eliminates the A→B vs B→A deadlock while preserving exact single-request semantics and throughput.
